title: WWT ↔ U.S. Army Signal Mapping
description: World Wide Technology public content and Army business, set next to U.S. Army leadership priorities.
readFirst: Covers Oct. 25–29. New: WWT said Oct. 28 at Cisco Partner Summit that it was named Global One Cisco Partner of the Year, and the release also lists a U.S. Federal Defense Partner of the Year award. The Oct. 20 Secure AI specialization and the Oct. 21 Polarise and DDN items were removed because they are older than seven days. The two Signal Mapping notes are analysis, tagged Inference. No WWT press release dated Oct. 29 was found.

items.headline: WWT is named Global One Cisco Partner of the Year, and Federal Defense Partner of the Year
items.summary: WWT said Oct. 28 at Cisco Partner Summit in Vancouver that it was named Global One Cisco Partner of the Year, and also Global Enterprise, Global Americas, and Global Networking Partner of the Year. The release lists a U.S. Federal Defense Partner of the Year award among the Americas honors, and says Softchoice, a WWT company, was named Canada Security Partner of the Year and Central Canada Impact Partner of the Year. Tim Coogan, Cisco's senior vice president of global partner sales, said he was recognizing WWT as the 2026 Global One Cisco Partner of the Year. Bob Olwig, WWT's executive vice president for global partner alliances, tied the awards to Cisco Global Partner status and the Secure Networking and Secure AI Infrastructure specializations.

items.headline: MeriTalk: the Army named WWT and AWS for the Project Griffin cyber pilot
items.summary: MeriTalk reported Oct. 26 that the Army selected World Wide Technology and Amazon Web Services for a combined $2.6 million pilot under Project Griffin. MeriTalk says the pilot is meant to advance AI-enabled cyber defense and that Griffin is one of three accelerated efforts under Project ARDS, the Army Rapid Defensive of Cyber Systems initiative. Principal cyber advisor Brandon Pugh said the Army will implement what he called SI-enabled tools to detect, divert and deceive threat actors and to scale network defense.

items.headline: TechNet Indo-Pacific: WWT listed GEMSS office hours in Honolulu for Oct. 26
items.summary: WWT lists an Oct. 26, 1:00 p.m. session at the Hilton Hawaiian Village during AFCEA TechNet Indo-Pacific. The advertised topics are Cisco software entitlements under GEMSS 2.1, Enterprise Agreement+ customer success, Cisco certification training, Cisco Advanced Services for the Army, and a SPINNAKER demonstration. AUSA itself ended Oct. 14.

items.headline: Griffin is a new cyber pilot with WWT's name on it; it is not the GEMSS Cisco vehicle
items.summary: MeriTalk's Oct. 26 report says the Army selected WWT and AWS for a $2.6 million Project Griffin pilot aimed at an agentic cyber-defense platform. The Army Cisco agreement WWT posted in July is GEMSS 2.1, the enterprise software and support consolidation. Nothing in the MeriTalk report says Griffin changes GEMSS, names a Cisco bill of materials, or makes WWT an NGC2 prime. Read together, the new public line that names WWT is a small cyber pilot, and the Cisco vehicle WWT has published is a separate enterprise agreement.

items.headline: Gatekeeper is a new software prescreen; it does not replace GEMSS as the Army Cisco vehicle
items.summary: The Army's Oct. 25 release says Project Gatekeeper launched Oct. 23 so a vendor with a Department of War CAC can submit code to an isolated sandbox and get automated security feedback before an authority to operate. WWT's only Army agreement still posted as current news is GEMSS 2.1, the July Cisco enterprise software and support consolidation. Nothing in the Gatekeeper release names WWT or changes that agreement. The new path is a prescreen for commercial software on the Army network; public Login.gov access is not available yet, and the funded Cisco footprint on the record is unchanged.
